name: CapCut Staggered Blur Glitch Text Reveal
use_when: A short title or phrase needs a stylized social reveal with separate words landing in sequence.
The subject looks or moves into the text area and the reveal can be timed to that action.
The edit can use a brief glitch cue without making speech or tone feel cheap.
avoid_when: The line is a continuous subtitle or accessibility caption.
The words are too long to stagger without losing reading order.
A glitch sound would fight the tone, dialogue, or music.
The blur makes the final word slower to read than plain text.

timeline_pattern.pattern: separate_word_layers -> position_as_phrase -> move_2_frames_in -> blade_all_layers -> recolor_pre_reveal_segments -> stagger_word_starts -> compound_each_word -> add_blur_effect_segments -> align_trimmed_glitch_sfx -> qc
timeline_pattern.stagger_rule: Offset each word slightly to the right on the timeline so the phrase reveals in a readable order.
timeline_pattern.pre_reveal_rule: A brief alternate-color pre-reveal segment can create style, but it should last only a few frames.
timeline_pattern.compound_rule: Compound each word before adding blur so the blur follows that word's reveal timing cleanly.
timeline_pattern.sound_rule: Trim the glitch cue to end exactly when the staggered reveal finishes.

motion.rule: The reveal should feel quick and intentional, then resolve into stable readable text.

keyframe_values.initial_blade: Move about 2 frames from the start before blading all word layers for a fast pre-reveal color flash.
keyframe_values.blur_high: A blur value around 25 can work for the heavier pre-reveal or transition segment.
keyframe_values.blur_low: A blur value around 4 can work as the cleaner resolving segment before the word becomes stable.
keyframe_values.stagger: Stagger each word only far enough to create rhythm; stop before the phrase becomes hard to assemble.

sound.rule: Use one short glitch or tick family cue aligned to the first word reveal and cut at the final word reveal; keep it below speech.

captions.rule: Suppress duplicate captions while the designed staggered phrase carries the same words; restore captions after the reveal clears.

color.rule: The pre-reveal color should contrast with the final color without becoming a random accent that changes the meaning.

implementation.ffmpeg: Render separate drawtext layers with staggered enable times, brief color changes, optional blur/fade expressions, and a trimmed glitch SFX mixed below dialogue; move longer sequences to Remotion or ASS.
implementation.remotion: Represent each word as a layer with startFrame, delayFrames, preRevealFrames, preColor, finalColor, blurFrom, blurTo, seeded glitch jitter if needed, and shared glitchSfxRange.
implementation.blender: Use separate text objects with staggered visibility/material changes and compositor blur; place the glitch cue in the edit timeline.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Create separate text layers, position the phrase, blade all words around 2 frames in, recolor the first small segments, stagger the word clips, compound each word, add a blur effect with stronger blur near the reveal and lower blur as it resolves, then add and trim a glitch SFX to the reveal span.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics word layers or nests, stagger starts, animate color/blur or use a tested blur preset, and trim a glitch SFX to the reveal duration.

common_mistakes: Staggering words so far apart that the viewer cannot read the phrase as one idea.
Leaving the red or alternate-color pre-reveal onscreen too long.
Using blur values that make the final text muddy.
Letting the glitch SFX tail continue after the reveal is complete.
Applying the effect to many lines until no title moment feels special.
qc: Is the final phrase readable at phone size after the stagger resolves?
Does the staggered order match the intended reading order?
Does blur clear before the viewer needs the words?
Does the glitch SFX end with the final visible reveal and stay below speech?
Do captions, faces, proof, UI, products, and action remain safe?
